answer: A scripted farm hence has to pad 59 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. Because the timing is recorded against the relic challenge, the kernel audit can replay the jade history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 233 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
